# Expected output — `tests/fixtures/secret_scan/release/`

Hand-written ground truth for `analysis/secret_scan.py`. These are the values
`tests/test_secret_scan.py` asserts. Nothing here was generated by the scanner.

The strings in `findings.csv` are synthetic. The `ghp_…` value is a sequential
placeholder that matches the GitHub-token *shape* only; it is not, and never
was, a credential.

## `clean.csv`

No findings, in any column.

## `findings.csv`

All findings fall in the `note` column. The `repo` column matches nothing.

| Pattern | Severity | Distinct matches | Matched text |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `email` | REVIEW | 1 | `maintainer@example.com` |
| `github_token` | BLOCKER | 1 | `ghp_0123456789abcdefghijABCDEFGHIJ012345` |
| `internal_host` | REVIEW | 1 | `build01.corp` |

`bearer_token` does not fire on this fixture.

`internal_host` is REVIEW, not BLOCKER: on the real `release/v0.1` bundle every
one of its six matches is a harvested public identifier (`jdk.internal`,
`Dockerfile.local`, and four like them), so gating on it would fail every build
on noise. See the module docstring of `analysis/secret_scan.py`.

## Whole-directory run

| | |
|---|---:|
| files scanned | 2 |
| BLOCKER findings | 1 |
| REVIEW findings | 2 |

`--limit 1` scans `clean.csv` alone, because files are sorted by path before
the limit is applied, so a limited run is a prefix of the full run and not an
arbitrary sample.
